title: Why Are AI GameDevs Only Releasing On Itch?
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
I put together this form for an AI Game Festival to create awareness around AI Game devs and some struck me as really weird:

  
30 entries so far, **only 2** are on Steam. Vast majority on Itch, followed by their own sites.

Why is this?

Is it because Steam cost too much? Not understanding distribution growth? Fear of being hated on Steam? Something else?

replies.author: ByerN
replies.body:
>Hassle is the same.

Not really. This is what it looks like:

Publishing on itchio:

* name the game,
* drop a zip file,
* done

Publishing on Steam:

* pay 100$,
* name the game,
* setup steam page, capsule arts, descriptions, hw requirements, other things from the first checklist,
* send your steam page to review,
* wait 3-7 days,
* review failed because there is not enough text/too much text in the wrong place/some other random thing in the capsule,
* fix and send your steam page to review again,
* wait 2-5 days,
* review failed because you used an in-game asset in your capsule or whatever thing you are not allowed to do,
* fix and send your steam page to review again,
* wait 2-5 days,
* review passed,
* complete second checklist (for your build)
* send your build for review,
* wait 3-7 days,
* review failed because your library asset is wrong or whatever other random thing,
* fix send your build for review,
* wait 2-5 days,
* review passed,
* wanna do a demo and/or playtest before releasing your game?
   * Yes - repeat all steps for each of them
   * No - ignore
* are you releasing demo?
   * Yes - don't forget to check this one small hidden checkbox that prevents your demo button from appearing on the game page, and you won't know about it for the first time,
   * No - ignore
* wanna add 50 achievements?
   * Yes - add them all one by one, or write a script that does it for you
   * No - ignore
* release your game,
* done

I ignored setting up your publisher account + payment info.

replies.author: Beneficial_Bid_5859
replies.body:
I get that. Their heart is in the right place.  

But they ironically are causing the very thing they oppose.  I have a BS in computer Science, I am a professional.  Im just crossing domains with full disclosure.  My win, is my kids being part of something that is on Steam for them to be proud of.  If someone buys a copy, cool, their college funds could use a boost.  If not, I learned more about a new domain than I knew before.  Is the game in a rough state, yes, is it resource wasteful, could be, its literally a few weeks old while also working a 50 hour work week and raising a family.  The point is that in the right hands AI can be very good, maybe my hands aren’t the right hands. But clearly this is a lot more than most first timers produce in a few weeks.  

my use of AI does not take food from a developer or artists mouth.  In fact the assets I purchased did the opposite.  So worst case scenario, I sell zero copies, some artists got some money, my kids have something to remember, I’ve already won. 

As a person whose job is literally at risk right now from AI and cheap labor, maliciously trying to stop me, is worse than suits laying people off, suits aren’t actively trying to be malicious, just being logical based on their parameters. 

Thank you for your comment

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
A better question is why are they releasing it to a platform like itch and Steam at all.

A lot of people in this space are completely deluded. 

Before AI, most game devs would spend years working on their games and 99% of them are unsuccessful. Now people think they can just throw together a game using AI in a month and slap it online to make money.

All that's actually happening is that people are flooding these platforms with slop. For every one game that's good there's 50 more slop games that are nothing more than a concept demo or the fun for 2 minutes type of games.

People on Steam are more adverse to slop because about 10 years or so back Steam had the great asset flip flood where every other game on Steam was asset flip slop. That's exactly the reason they started charging per game listing as it use to be per account.

Imo it's only a matter of time before platforms like itch crack down on it as it's being flooded with low effort AI content now.

Nothing wrong with having fun making games with AI but unless you have a really polished finished game people shouldn't be uploading to these platforms. With the amount of slop being uploaded nobody or very few people are even going to see your game anyway let alone play or pay for it.

By uploading half assed and obvious looking AI games to these platforms all it's going to achieve is making more people hate AI and more platforms making it harder to publish to them.

replies.author: Beneficial_Bid_5859
replies.body:
Its not AI that makes the slop. Its the architect.  

AI is a junior developer, if u dont know how to manage junior devs and impose patterns and arch on them ur sunk from the start.  Its no different with people either.  Give me 4 junior devs ill crank solid apps quickly.  Put 4 junior devs in a room with no architect, and grab ur slop bowls, cuz its gonna rain. 

In many ways the AI is better than people, because it takes corrective feedback and is honest.  People will cling to a bad idea to save face all the way to the grave.  

So, ya there is alot of AI generated slop, but there is so much more human made slop. U should see many of these major companies relation db’s for example. Many lack pks and fks, invented when seat belts and air conditioners were options in cars.  Wtf in 2026 makes a db table without keys?  But the user doesn’t see that slop, they just feel the consequences. 

Same thing can be said when we went to downloading games instead of buying them in a box on a shelf at walmart.  Those games were complete, no way to fix them after release.  Now its, send what u got, we will patch and hot fix later…….  Its not AI that makes slop, its people, dumb people.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
I'm not saying AI creates slop. It's always people that create slop. As far as I'm concerned it's human slop. AI is just the tool people are using to produce it.

The problem with AI is that it now enables humans to create slop on an industrial scale never seen before and it's only going to get worse. People in the AI community should be trying to discourage that not encourage.

Nearly every day there's a post here from someone complaining about anti AI people. Many of them are like that because they are seeing the amount of low effort content currently flooding platforms.

Unfortunately AI is an easy tool to abuse and many people on the pro AI side like to turn a blind eye to the problems.

It's like people going to a picnic spot to eat and drink. You might be be taking your trash home with you but if 50 people for every one person doing that are just leaving their trash all over the place then soon a lot of people will become anti picnics.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Are you a Game Dev using AI to make games?  

Do you think that only people who've spent years learning how to use Blender and Unity etc should be able to make games?  

I have aphantasia (look it up if you don't know what it is) - I cannot visualise anything in my mind, I can't even picture my parents or sister's faces.  Without AI there is no way I could make a game.

It doesn't matter if the game was built using AI, or uses AI art, what matters is if the game is actually playable. 

Personally I hate most AAA games because they require too much time.  I much prefer fast loading, quick to play arcade style games.
